## Background

We will perform PCA of protein structureal data from the PDB.

`get.seq()` - input database identifier 
`blast.pdb()` or `get.pdb()` - find and dowload structures
`pdbaln()` - align and superpose structures
`pca()` - score plot


## Set-up

let's load all the packages we're gonnna need FIRST.

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
library(bio3d)
library(bio3dview)
library(ggplot2)
#BiocManager::install("msa")
library(msa)
```


## Getting a sequence

Starting with a single sequence ID.

```{r}
id <- "1ake_A"
```

```{r}
aa <- get.seq(id)
aa
```


> Q10. Which of the packages above is found only on BioConductor and not CRAN? 

> Q11. Which of the above packages is not found on BioConductor or CRAN?: 

> Q12. True or False? Functions from the pak package can be used to install packages from GitHub and BitBucket? 

```{r}
# Blast or hmmer search 
#b <- blast.pdb(aa)

# List out some 'top hits'
#head(hits$pdb.id)
```

> If blast did not return results (likely due to the large number of simultaneous requests from the class) you can use the following vector of PDB IDs

```{r}
hits <- NULL
hits$pdb.id <- c('1AKE_A','6S36_A','6RZE_A','3HPR_A','1E4V_A','5EJE_A','1E4Y_A','3X2S_A','6HAP_A','6HAM_A','4K46_A','3GMT_A','4PZL_A')

# Download releated PDB files
files <- get.pdb(hits$pdb.id, path="pdbs", split=TRUE, gzip=TRUE)

# Align releated PDBs
pdbs <- pdbaln(files, fit = TRUE, exefile="msa")

#view.pdbs(pdbs)
```


## PCA

```{r}
# Perform PCA
pc.xray <- pca(pdbs)
plot(pc.xray)
```

Looks like the first two PCs are plenty, cover 96% of variance.

```{r}
plot(pc.xray, 1:2)
```

```{r}
# view.pca(pc.xray)
```

Write a wee movie  (called a trajectory) for viewing in Mol* :

```{r}
mktrj(pc.xray, file="pca_result.pdb")
```
